updates.title: RBI 247 October: selected priority reading added
updates.body: Explained mechanisms and recall distinctions now cover banking liquidity, information sharing, capital, supervision, bonds, tokenisation and economic data. All 163 pages were machine-scanned; selected excerpts were curated. Consequential rules, statistical series and legal events remain unverified; see the verification holds within Read notes.

teaching_notes.title: October 2026: what is included and what is not verified
paragraphs: This chapter is an original explanation of selected priority material from RBI 247 October 2026. Start with liquidity, consent-based data sharing, prudential risk, bond-market risk and macro-data interpretation. These overlap strongly with banking GA, Finance and ESI. The full file has 163 pages; a machine scan covered them all, but the curated notes use selected article excerpts. Practice questions and their supplied solutions are not reproduced.

A monthly compilation is not the RBI, SEBI, the Gazette or an official statistical release. The contents include consequential claims about new rules, a bank's licence, payment charges and revised statistical series. Those are not independently authenticated here. Understand the mechanisms below, but do not treat an unverified number or legal event as today's operative rule. The verification-hold table separates the most sensitive claims from the normal recall list.

The policy section describes an inflation aim as '4%-6%' without explaining the target versus tolerance distinction. That wording is not used as a teaching definition here. A target, a tolerance band, an observed inflation number and a forecast are different objects. No currently operative target/band is asserted without the relevant notification.

teaching_notes.title: 1. Monetary policy: rate decision, stance and corridor
paragraphs: The compilation reports an October repo-rate increase of 25 basis points to 5.50%, with SDF at 5.25% and MSF/Bank Rate at 5.75%, and describes a change in stance. These are source claims, not a verified current rate card. The safe concept is that a rate decision changes the price of central-bank liquidity, while a stance communicates the policy approach. A stance is not a promise that every future meeting must change rates in the same direction.

SDF and MSF help form the operating corridor around the policy repo rate: the deposit facility is associated with absorbing surplus liquidity and the marginal lending facility with banks obtaining funds under its conditions. A standing facility and the fixed reverse repo are not interchangeable just because both can appear in a rate table. Transmission to bank lending and spending depends on liquidity, funding costs, balance sheets and demand.

A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point. An invented increase from 5.25% to 5.50% is 25 basis points, or 0.25 percentage points, not a 25% interest-rate rise. The compilation also reports FY2026-27 real-growth and CPI forecasts of 7.1% and 5.2%; forecasts are conditional, not observed outcomes. Keep publisher, release and fiscal-year horizon together before using those values.

teaching_notes.title: 2. Account Aggregators: sharing information is not moving money
paragraphs: An Account Aggregator helps a customer access and share financial information with consent. A financial information provider holds the underlying information, for example a bank holding account data. Interoperability means the customer is not unnecessarily confined to one information-sharing channel. It does not mean every institution can view all of a person's accounts without permission.

The compilation describes interoperability among NBFC-AAs and inclusion of bank-deposit information in a Consolidated Account Statement through the AA framework. It gives 31 December 2026 as an expected implementation date. An expected date is not evidence that the arrangement is already operating everywhere. Viewing deposit information alongside investments does not transfer the deposit into the demat account or replace the bank's liability with a security.

Illustrative household has deposits at one bank and securities recorded through a depository. A consented consolidated view can help the household see its financial position, while each asset remains governed by its own institution and product terms. Exam trap: information sharing, lending approval, investment advice and movement of funds are distinct services. Better data can assist lending assessment without guaranteeing credit.

teaching_notes.title: 3. Bank ownership and cash handling: identify what actually changes
paragraphs: Large bank shareholdings matter because owners can influence institutions that take public deposits. The compilation describes a one-time approval route for eligible mutual funds, insurers and pension funds making subsequent major acquisitions. Simplifying repeat applications is not the same as removing ownership supervision or granting every investor unlimited control. Eligibility, approval conditions and holdings still require the actual directions.

Note sorting separates two questions: is a banknote genuine, and is it physically fit for recirculation? A genuine note can still be damaged. The compilation reports updated machinery directions and BIS-related requirements. Learn the authenticity-versus-fitness distinction rather than assuming a machine's acceptance makes a suspect note legally genuine.

ATM cassette swaps replace cash containers with prepared lockable cassettes rather than handling loose cash at the site. The reported October change concerns whether a committee of executives may monitor implementation instead of the Board itself. A change in the monitoring body does not by itself abolish the underlying cash-security requirement. Authority, process and deadline are separate fields in a regulatory question.

teaching_notes.title: 4. Daily CRR maintenance: percentage of a requirement, not a new CRR rate
paragraphs: CRR links a prescribed reserve balance to the relevant liability base; the minimum daily maintenance rule specifies how far daily balances may vary around the required reserve arrangement. These are two layers, not one percentage. The compilation reports minimum daily maintenance moving from 90% to 99% of required CRR from the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026. This is unverified and is not taught as an increase of the CRR rate to 99%.

Invented bank has required reserves of Rs 100 crore. A 90% daily floor would mean Rs 90 crore; a 99% floor would mean Rs 99 crore. The Rs 9 crore difference concerns flexibility on an individual day. It does not mean the fortnight's prescribed average automatically rises by Rs 9 crore. If NDTL and the prescribed CRR are unchanged, the reserve requirement and the daily flexibility remain distinct.

Reduced flexibility can affect daily liquidity management and demand for overnight funds, but an interest-rate or lending effect is not an accounting certainty. Judge the system's liquidity and banks' adjustment. Exam trap: the denominator is required CRR, not total deposits; daily minimum, fortnight average and the CRR/NDTL rate must not be interchanged.

teaching_notes.title: 5. Foreign-exchange support, swaps and derivative risk
paragraphs: Oil importers need foreign currency to pay overseas suppliers. The compilation describes a special dollar-supply window for named public-sector oil companies. Routing some demand through a central-bank facility can change pressure in the open market. It is not free foreign currency, a cancellation of the import bill or a guarantee of a fixed exchange rate.

A currency-swap facility is the arrangement under which access is possible; a drawdown is the amount actually used; rollover extends the existing funding under agreed terms. The Maldives item describes a Rs 3,000 crore drawdown extension. A rollover is not automatically a fresh grant of the same size, and a facility ceiling is not necessarily the amount outstanding.

A non-deliverable derivative settles a difference in value rather than exchanging the full principal currencies. Hedging offsets an underlying risk; speculation takes exposure to an anticipated movement. Notional principal is a reference amount, not the current loss or cash exchanged. The compilation's new NDDC restrictions and 20% FERR are held as unverified rule claims; do not extend them to every forex contract or infer actual capital from notional value.

teaching_notes.title: 6. Risk-weighted capital and leverage: two denominators
paragraphs: Prudential capital provides loss-absorption capacity. Under a risk-weighted approach, exposures are adjusted using applicable risk weights before the capital ratio is applied. The compilation describes a 2% risk weight for specified QCCP exposures. This is a source-specific claim and is not a statement that every derivative needs capital of 2% of its notional amount.

Invented exposure is Rs 100 crore and the assumed risk weight is 2%, producing Rs 2 crore of risk-weighted assets. If an illustrative capital requirement were 10%, capital associated with that calculation would be Rs 0.20 crore, not Rs 2 crore. The 10% is invented solely to explain the two steps; actual exposures, netting and capital requirements follow the applicable rules.

A leverage ratio uses a regulatory capital numerator against an exposure measure designed not to depend on the same risk weights. Off-balance-sheet commitments may require conversion into exposure, while derivatives and securities-financing transactions have their own treatment. A guarantee can create exposure even before cash is paid. Credit conversion factor, risk weight and required capital are different stages; do not merge them into one percentage.

teaching_notes.title: 7. Supervisory data, financial coordination and cyber resilience
paragraphs: Supervision relies on accurate, complete, timely and consistent information about banks' assets, funding and risk. The compilation's sDQI measures data quality, not a bank's credit rating or a direct probability of failure. It reports an overall score rising from 90.7 in March to 93.3 in June 2026; this is a dated unverified observation. An improved data-quality score does not prove that every underlying loan became safer.

CIMS reporting, including the described non-resident deposit returns, concerns the data pipeline. PRAVAAH is described as an application/approval interface, which is a different task. FSDC provides coordination across the financial system; it is not a replacement for each regulator's statutory responsibilities. Risks can cross sectors, making coordination important without merging all regulators into one.

The reported Bhubaneswar data centre and cybersecurity training institute illustrate service continuity and skills. Reliable backup capacity can help sustain critical systems, while training improves incident response. Announcing infrastructure or spending an amount is not proof of immunity from cyberattack. Exam trap: infrastructure availability, secure configuration, detection and recovery are complementary safeguards.

teaching_notes.title: 8. Credit Risk-o-Meter: disclosure does not remove investment risk
paragraphs: A bond exposes its holder to several risks. Credit risk concerns payment failure; market risk concerns adverse price movements; liquidity risk concerns selling quickly without a large concession. A visual credit indicator can make one dimension easier to recognise without describing every other risk.

The compilation describes a Credit Risk-o-Meter for specified debt instruments, including display of the lowest rating where there are multiple ratings and a separate indication of a non-cooperating issuer. These reported display requirements are not independently verified. The durable lesson is that selecting only the most favourable rating can conceal relevant credit information.

An Online Bond Platform Provider facilitates discovery, comparison and transactions in eligible debt securities. It is not automatically the issuer, the guarantor of repayment or an investment recommendation. A secured instrument still depends on collateral value, enforceability and cash flows; an AT1 or perpetual instrument may have additional loss-absorption features. Neither a colour code nor a platform listing makes a bond risk-free.

teaching_notes.title: 9. Bond futures, closing prices, IPO changes and surveillance
paragraphs: A corporate-bond index future can help offset some portfolio market risk. If a bond portfolio loses value as market yields rise, an appropriately designed futures position may partly offset the loss. It does not make the issuer repay, and differences between the portfolio and index create basis risk. The compilation describes a prospective exchange product; approval and actual launch/liquidity are different milestones.

CAS has two meanings in these notes: Consolidated Account Statement in the information context, and Closing Auction Session in equity trading. The reported closing auction concentrates orders to discover a closing price. A closing price is not automatically the settlement price used for every expiring derivative. Do not copy a timetable or VWAP rule across instruments without its scope.

An IPO fresh issue creates new shares and raises funds for the company; an offer for sale transfers existing holders' shares. A relaxation about changing fresh-issue size does not automatically apply to every IPO component. Similarly, an AI surveillance alert identifies a possible anomaly, not established fraud. A committee, code or investigation is a process, not proof of a final outcome.

teaching_notes.title: 10. Tokenisation and atomic settlement: faster exchange, not guaranteed value
paragraphs: Tokenisation represents a financial claim using a digital record. The bond remains an obligation of its issuer under its terms: changing the record-keeping technology does not by itself improve the issuer's cash flow or remove credit risk. The compilation describes a corporate-bond tokenisation pilot linked to wholesale digital rupee infrastructure.

Atomic settlement aims to make the security transfer and payment conditional on one another so that one side is not completed alone. Invented bond sale: buyer transfers Rs 10 lakh only as the corresponding bond is delivered. This addresses a settlement mismatch, not a fall in the bond's market value or failure of future interest payments.

Do not confuse wholesale CBDC used in settlement with every retail programmable-payment use case. A pilot is evidence of testing a mechanism, not universal market deployment or a finding that custody, operational, legal and cyber risks have all disappeared.

teaching_notes.title: 11. NBFC asset quality: a ratio can improve for more than one reason
paragraphs: Loans are assets of a lender because they are expected to produce payments. Gross NPAs measure classified problem loans before the specified adjustments for provisions. GNPA ratio = gross NPAs / gross advances x 100. The classification rules depend on the product and applicable regulatory framework; a general term-loan overdue threshold should not be used indiscriminately for every exposure.

The compilation reports NBFC GNPA of 2.4% in FY26 compared with 6.1% during a 2018 stress reference. These are unverified and the periods are not a complete time series. A lower ratio can result from recoveries, write-offs, reclassification or growth in the denominator. It does not alone identify which mechanism improved or whether risk is equally distributed.

Invented lender has NPAs of 30 and gross loans of 1,000, so GNPA is 3%. If loans rise to 1,500 with NPAs still 30, the ratio falls to 2% without a reduction in the problem-loan stock. Read stocks, flows and provisions alongside the ratio. New lending may also have had less time to reveal repayment stress.

teaching_notes.title: 12. Inflation and output data: index level, annual change and revision
paragraphs: An index compares a measured level with a reference base; an inflation or production-growth rate compares two periods. Rebasing can change coverage and weights, so numbers from different series cannot simply be spliced. The compilation asserts new WPI/Output PPI and CPI bases and includes an expanded IIP sector table; those series descriptions are not independently authenticated here.

The September CPI table reports combined inflation of 5.54% and an index of 109.49. If these source values are used as a practice case, 109.49 means 9.49% above its stated base, not 9.49% annual inflation. Computing annual inflation requires the comparable September index a year earlier, not just the previous month's index.

The policy section rounds August CPI to 4.8% while the detailed table gives 4.83%. This can be rounding rather than a contradiction; preserve precision and provisional/final status. The WPI section reports 9.92% for August and 11.39% for September, a 1.47 percentage-point change, not 1.47% growth in the index. Do not turn these unauthenticated figures or base-year assertions into official recall facts.

teaching_notes.title: 13. Tax and fiscal news: scope, legal stage and denominator
paragraphs: An export levy affects specified exports; a change in it does not automatically change domestic fuel taxes or pump prices. A GST Council recommendation may still need legislation or notification before it changes the legal rule. A form for a specified investor exemption does not make all government-security income tax-free. The compilation's exact new form and tax-law claims remain unverified.

The fiscal item reports an April-September deficit of Rs 7.14 lakh crore as 42.1% of the annual budget target, while separately quoting a 4.3%-of-GDP annual target. The two percentages have different denominators. Reaching 42.1% of a target is not a deficit of 42.1% of GDP and is not, on its own, a breach of the annual target.

The rounded receipt and spending tables do not reconcile exactly: 25.50 minus 18.35 is 7.15, not the headline 7.14 lakh crore, and component receipts sum to 18.36. This may involve rounding or differing coverage; reconcile the original release before a precise calculation. Revenues and expenditure are seasonal, so half-year progress should not simply be doubled into a prediction of the full year.

tables.title: October finance: facts and confusable distinctions

cells: Account Aggregator
Consent-based financial-information access/sharing; not a transfer of deposits or automatic loan sanction.
Concept, not proof of current implementation.
October 2026 edition
CAS: consolidated information
The compilation describes bank-deposit information being added to a Consolidated Account Statement through AAs.
Expected 31 December 2026 implementation is a source claim, not achieved coverage.
October 2026 edition
CAS: two expansions
Consolidated Account Statement concerns holdings; Closing Auction Session concerns price discovery.
Do not transfer a timing or operational rule from one CAS to the other.
October 2026 edition
Bank shareholding approval
Eligible mutual funds, insurers and pension funds are named for a reported one-time subsequent-acquisition approval route.
Unverified amendment; not an unconditional exemption for every investor.
October 2026 edition
Banknote sorting
Authenticity and physical fitness are separate tests: genuine does not necessarily mean fit to recirculate.
Machinery certification and phase-out dates require the applicable directions.
October 2026 edition
ATM cassette-swap monitoring
The reported change concerns monitoring by a committee of executives; the cash-security mechanism is a separate requirement.
Unverified October circular, not removal of cassette swaps.
October 2026 edition
Daily CRR floor versus prescribed CRR
The compilation reports 90% to 99% daily maintenance of required CRR, not a CRR rate of 99% of NDTL.
Unverified rule; reported start is fortnight beginning 16 October 2026.
October 2026 edition
CIMS versus PRAVAAH
CIMS receives regulatory data; PRAVAAH handles regulatory applications, licences and permissions in the described workflow.
Reporting data is not the same as obtaining approval.
October 2026 edition
Risk weight versus capital
Exposure x risk weight gives risk-weighted exposure; the applicable capital requirement is then applied.
Reported 2% QCCP risk weight is not capital equal to 2% of every trade.
October 2026 edition
CCF versus risk weight
A credit conversion factor converts a contingent/off-balance-sheet commitment into exposure; risk weighting is a different step.
Product-specific rules and the leverage exposure measure must be distinguished.
October 2026 edition
Securities-financing transactions
Repo, reverse repo and securities lending can generate counterparty exposure.
Collateral reduces some risks; it does not establish zero counterparty risk.
October 2026 edition
Supervisory Data Quality Index
Accuracy, completeness, timeliness and consistency concern quality of banks' supervisory reporting.
Not a credit rating or proof that all underlying bank risk fell.
October 2026 edition
FSDC
Coordinates financial-stability discussion across authorities rather than replacing their individual mandates.
The reported 30th meeting and chair/event details are unverified.
October 2026 edition
Data centre and cybersecurity training
The reported RBI Bhubaneswar initiative connects continuity of critical systems with professional cyber capability.
Inauguration/spending is not proof of immunity to cyber incidents.
October 2026 edition
Corporate-bond index futures
Can hedge some bond-portfolio market exposure but do not guarantee issuer repayment or eliminate basis risk.
A proposed or approved product is not proof of actual trading liquidity.
October 2026 edition
AI surveillance
Automated analysis can flag unusual corporate filings for further investigation.
An alert is not a finding of fraud; described model development is not universal deployment.
October 2026 edition
Brand promotion versus product claim
The supplied advertisement-code item distinguishes promotion of an entity/brand from specific product inducements.
Unverified legal framework; celebrity promotion does not establish suitability.
October 2026 edition
Credit Risk-o-Meter
A credit-risk display does not measure every market or liquidity risk or recommend an investment.
Scope is the specified debt instrument, not all financial assets.
October 2026 edition
Multiple credit ratings
The compilation says the lowest applicable credit rating must be shown rather than selecting only the best one.
Unverified display requirement; INC is an additional disclosure condition.
October 2026 edition
Online Bond Platform Provider
Facilitates eligible bond discovery and transactions, distinct from issuing the debt or guaranteeing repayment.
Access and disclosure do not remove credit, liquidity or market risk.
October 2026 edition
Fresh issue versus offer for sale
Fresh issue raises money for the issuer; sale of existing holders' shares transfers their ownership.
Reported size-relaxation percentages/deadlines are not independently verified.
October 2026 edition
Tokenisation
Digital representation of a bond claim changes record/transaction mechanics, not the issuer's repayment obligation.
A pilot is not universal market deployment.
October 2026 edition
Atomic settlement
Security transfer and payment are linked to avoid completing only one leg.
Does not eliminate bond default risk or every operational risk.
October 2026 edition
GNPA ratio
Gross NPAs divided by gross advances x 100; a falling ratio can reflect denominator growth as well as recoveries.
FY26 2.4% is a supplied claim, not authenticated current NBFC performance.
October 2026 edition

tables.title: October finance: facts and confusable distinctions

cells: Forecast versus realised GDP
A projection for FY2026-27 is not an observed annual growth result.
Reported GDP 7.1% and CPI 5.2% forecasts remain unverified.
FY2026-27 forecast in October 2026 compilation
Index level versus annual inflation
An index of 109.49 indicates a level relative to its base; it does not by itself establish annual inflation.
September CPI/base-year claims require original-release verification.
September 2026 provisional, as labelled in source
Provisional versus final data
Initial estimates can change as more data arrive; compare the same reference period and series.
August 4.8% versus 4.83% can be rounding, not a substantive conflict.
August/September 2026, source-era series
Export tax versus domestic fuel tax
A cut to a specified petroleum export levy does not automatically cut domestic pump-price taxes.
Reported reintroduction/current export rates are unverified.
October 2026 compilation
GST recommendation versus law
Council recommendations and proposals do not by themselves establish that amended penalties or procedures are operative.
Use legal stage/effective date; no new threshold is endorsed here.
October 2026 compilation
Tax form versus universal exemption
An exemption process for specified investors is not proof that all holders of government securities pay no tax.
New Form 173A/ordinance details are held for verification.
October 2026 compilation
Share of annual deficit target
A percentage of a budget target has a different denominator from deficit/GDP.
Reported 42.1% is not 42.1% of GDP or proof of a target breach.
April-September FY2026-27
Reconcile fiscal tables
Rounded headline deficit and receipts/expenditure can differ; check scope and precision before calculation.
25.50 - 18.35 = 7.15, versus a 7.14 headline; no reconciliation invented.
April-September FY2026-27
